key_insight: Raising the O2/C2H2 flame-spraying ratio densified Ni–Cr–B–Si self-fluxing coatings, lowering porosity and roughness while improving adhesion, with peak hardness at an intermediate ratio.
engineering_relevance: Tuning flame-spray gas ratio is a practical control knob for optimizing wear- and corrosion-resistant coating performance on AISI 321 steel.
method: Flame-sprayed Ni–Cr–B–Si self-fluxing coatings onto AISI 321 stainless steel
Varied O2/C2H2 ratio at 1.0, 1.1, and 1.2 using a Metal Coat 6PM-II system
Monitored spraying conditions with Accuraspray 4.0 and measured microstructure, porosity, hardness, roughness, and adhesion
evidence_signal: At O2/C2H2 = 1.2, porosity dropped to 0.90 ± 0.09% and adhesion rose to 35.02 ± 3.9 MPa, while the highest microhardness, 1051.7 HV, occurred at 1.1.
watch_item: The abstract reports a narrow process window and limited condition set, so broader validation is needed before generalizing to other substrates or spray systems.
paper_title: EFFECT OF FLAME-SPRAYING TEMPERATURE ON THE PROPERTIES OF Ni–Cr–B–Si-BASED SELF-FLUXING COATINGS
